claim: In its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results on 25 November 2026, Deere & Company forecasts fiscal 2027 net income (midpoint of its range) above the net income it reports for fiscal 2026.

runs.reason:
**Base rate:** Deere’s fiscal Q4 releases from 2020 through 2025 all gave a dollar range for next-year net income attributable to Deere. The midpoint was above the reported full-year result in three of six releases: 2020–2022 were YES on the earnings comparison, and 2023–2025 were NO. That gives a 50% starting point, though the streaks suggest the equipment cycle matters more than the raw frequency. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000155837020014042/de-20201125xex99d1.htm?utm_source=openai))

**What moves this case:**
- **Toward YES:** On August 20, Deere’s CEO reiterated that he saw fiscal 2026 as the bottom of the agricultural equipment cycle, citing early orders and improving used-equipment inventories. Construction & Forestry operating profit also rose to $436 million from $237 million in Q3, giving Deere a path to higher earnings even if large-ag demand only stabilizes. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))
- **Mixed:** The November 10 industry report showed October U.S. four-wheel-drive tractor sales up 7.7% year over year, but combine sales down 9.6%. Purdue’s November 3 survey showed an improvement in its Farm Capital Investment Index, but only 20% of respondents said it was a good time to invest in machinery and buildings. That supports stabilization more than a broad rebound. ([aem.org](https://www.aem.org/getattachment/261c39e3-982c-4da8-af96-5a7e90e2b952/October-2026-Farm_Flash_Trade_Press_With_Chart_PreRelease-Unitied-States.pdf))
- **Toward NO:** Deere’s August fiscal 2026 outlook was $4.75–$5.00 billion, and it had already recorded $382 million in tariff recoveries through nine months. If those recoveries do not recur, operating earnings must improve just to offset that benefit before the fiscal 2027 midpoint can clear the reported fiscal 2026 figure. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/315189/000110465926098904/de-20260820xex99d1.htm))

**Release-window risk:** Deere confirmed a 9 a.m. Central earnings call for November 25, 2026, in its November 11 announcement. I put the chance that the release misses the specified Central-time window at about 1%. An on-time release without dollar net-income guidance would also resolve NO, but Deere’s six-for-six disclosure record makes that a secondary risk. ([deere.com](https://www.deere.com/en-us/john-deere-news/fy26-q4-announcement?utm_source=openai))

### 3. Strongest Reason the Obvious Outcome Might Fail
While consensus expects FY2027 net income around $5.91 billion against roughly $4.90 billion in FY2026, Deere is historically conservative with its initial November full-year guidance (for instance, on November 26, 2025, it guided FY2026 to $4.0–$4.75 billion vs. $5.19 billion expected). Furthermore, FY2026 reported GAAP net income includes $382 million in one-time tariff refunds through Q3, and if Q4 FY2026 comes in at the high end of expectations (e.g., bringing full-year FY2026 net income to ~$5.00 billion or $5.05 billion) while management issues an ultra-conservative initial FY2027 range like $4.60 billion to $5.10 billion (midpoint $4.85 billion) due to the absence of tariff refunds and lingering weakness in farmer spending, the midpoint would fall slightly below reported FY2026 net income. (The chance that Deere fails to publish its results on November 25, 2026, or omits its standard dollar net-income outlook is negligible, under 1%).

Overall, given management's explicit framing of FY2026 as the bottom of the cycle, rising model-year 2027 early orders, strong Construction & Forestry growth, and a massive ~$1.0 billion buffer between expected FY2026 net income (~$4.90B) and consensus FY2027 net income ($5.91B), Deere is highly likely to guide to a FY2027 midpoint above its reported FY2026 net income, though a roughly 22% chance remains that an upside Q4 surprise combined with ultra-cautious initial guidance results in a flat or slightly lower midpoint.
